name: Scanner_Progression_System
description: How the scanner upgrades over time: radius upgrades, scan-time reduction, new detection categories (fossils, minerals, lifeforms), durability system, and knowledge-tier unlocks tied to player XP.

questions.question: Does scanner progression unlock deeper science (surface-ID -> composition analysis -> formation history)?
Can the progression system be shown as a compelling Steam trailer hook: 'Scan rocks -> unlock geology PhD'?
Does scanner progression feel like real scientific instrument advancement (bigger dish = more data), not a game-y skill tree?
Can progression be shipped incrementally (v1: radius only, v2: new categories, v3: composition analysis)?
Does progression depend on a player XP/level system (does that system exist yet)?
Does the upgrade system work in UE5.8 using existing GameplayAbilitySystem or custom UpgradeComponent?
Does tracking scan count, categories unlocked, and upgrade tiers add measurable save-game overhead?
Can a player who only scans occasionally still unlock meaningful upgrades (casual vs completionist pacing)?
Do scanner upgrades have distinct unlock sounds (new category unlocked, radius increased) that reward progression?
Do players share scanner progression or is each player's scanner independent in co-op?
Can modders define new upgrade tiers, categories, and unlock conditions through data tables?
Are upgrade descriptions, category names, and unlock notifications localizable without code changes?
Does the progression system depend on the Player_Progression/XP feature being built first?
Does this prove that educational content can be gated rewardingly (progression = deeper science) without frustrating?
Was this derived from Educational_Scanner Q4 (scan radius/time/durability as upgradable properties)?
Does gating science behind progression conflict with the educational mission (player must scan a lot before learning deep geology)?
What C++/Blueprint systems are needed (upgrade component, save-game tier storage, XP hooks)?
Does this need sub-sub-features (Upgrade_Tree, Category_Unlocks, Knowledge_Tiers) or are 26 Qs enough?
Are sibling progression features missing (e.g., Scanner_Recipe_Unlocks, Scanner_Crafting)?
Is Educational_Scanner designed enough to finalize progression (ATool_Scanner Durability/ScanRadius/ScanTime properties stable)?
Should progression be designed before or after the base scan mechanic works (progression depends on base scan existing)?
Does progression block other scanner features, or do UI/audio need to be built before progression can be shown?
Does a meaningful progression system (unlock deeper science through scanning) serve 'most famous educational RPG'?
What is sacrificed by making progression scan-count-based vs XP-based (casual players vs depth)?
What evidence shows that gating educational content behind progression (KSP tech tree) increases motivation vs open access?
Does the progression chain reach PLAYER MASTERY (player earns deeper knowledge through curiosity) or is it just a grind loop?
